question: During a basic vehicle controls skills test exercise, your vehicle's final position should be:
option_a: In the general area that was described by the examiner.
option_b: In the exact final position described by the examiner.
option_c: Within three feet of the final position described by the examiner.
explanation: You should finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position described by the examiner. You can be penalized for failing to complete an exercise exactly in the manner described by the examiner, potentially resulting in failure of the basic control skills test.

question: When making a stop to pick up students, a driver should ensure all surrounding traffic has stopped before:
option_a: Opening the door and signaling for the students to approach.
option_b: Turning on the alternating red lights.
option_c: Pulling over to the side of the road.
explanation: When stopping to pick up students, a school bus driver should ensure that all surrounding traffic has stopped before opening the door and signaling for the students to approach the bus.

question: A school bus's danger zones are located:
option_a: Only to the front of the bus.
option_b: Only to the rear and left side of the bus.
option_c: To the front, sides, and rear of the bus.
explanation: The danger zones of a school bus are areas in which children are most likely to be hit, either by another vehicle or by the bus itself. Such areas are located to the front, sides, and rear of a bus. Danger zones can extend 10 feet from every side of a bus.

question: If a student is believed to have suffered a back injury, you should:
option_a: Move them off the bus.
option_b: Not move them.
option_c: Encourage them to try to stand.
explanation: A school bus driver should not attempt to move a student who has suffered a neck or spinal injury unless the student's life is in immediate danger.

question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:
option_a: The brake pedal sticks.
option_b: The gas pedal is loose.
option_c: The grooved pedal surface has not been smoothed out.
explanation: When checking your vehicle's pedals during a pre-trip inspection, you should ensure that there is nothing under or around the pedals that will obstruct their use. Make sure the pedals are in proper working condition and that the surfaces of the pedals are grooved, if applicable.

question: When completing an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:
option_a: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
option_b: Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
option_c: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
explanation: If you are asked to complete an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should first pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the boundaries of the parking space.

question: When a school bus is approaching a bus stop, the driver should:
option_a: Not use the mirrors.
option_b: Approach with caution.
option_c: Drive quickly and stop abruptly.
explanation: School bus drivers should approach stops slowly and cautiously.

question: With the exception of the straight line backing exercise, a driver may exit their vehicle and check its position during testing exercises up to:
option_a: One time.
option_b: Two times.
option_c: Three times.
explanation: A driver is allowed to exit their vehicle to check its position during any basic vehicle control skills test exercise. This action is called a "look." During the straight line backing exercise, a driver may not exceed one look. During any other exercise, a driver may not exceed two looks.

question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:
option_a: Honk the horn.
option_b: Drive slowly.
option_c: Talk to students on the bus.
explanation: A school bus driver should always approach bus stops slowly and cautiously.

question: Bus stops may be changed by:
option_a: The driver.
option_b: Parents.
option_c: The school district.
explanation: Official school bus routes and stops are established by the local school district. Drivers should never change a stop location without the written approval of an appropriate district official.

question: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors allow you to see all of the following, except:
option_a: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
option_b: The area in front of the bus.
option_c: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors on a school bus should allow the driver to see the entire area in front of the bus, from the front bumper at ground level to a point where direct vision is possible. The mirrors should also display the right and left front tires touching the ground, as well as the area from the front of the bus to the service door.

question: For a basic vehicle control skills test, you are expected to be able to:
option_a: Alley dock.
option_b: Weave between a line of cones.
option_c: Complete an emergency stop.
explanation: Maneuvers that may be included in the basic vehicle control skills test include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look is when:
option_a: A driver checks the gauges on their instrument panel.
option_b: A driver checks their blind spots.
option_c: A driver walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.
explanation: A driver uses a look when they open their door, leave their seated position, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During the straight line backing exercise, a driver may not exceed one look. During any other exercise, a driver may not exceed two looks.

question: If a school bus stalls on a railroad track:
option_a: Students should remain on the bus.
option_b: Students should be evacuated to a location near the bus.
option_c: Students should be evacuated and moved away from the bus.
explanation: If a school bus becomes stalled or trapped on railroad tracks, the driver should immediately evacuate everyone from the bus. If the bus is struck by a train, to avoid any flying debris, the students should be led far away from the bus at an angle that is in the direction of any oncoming train.

question: Loading and unloading a bus:
option_a: Can be hazardous for passengers.
option_b: Does not need to be supervised.
option_c: Should be done while refueling.
explanation: More students are killed each year during loading or unloading of school buses than while riding on school buses. Therefore, it is critical that school bus drivers follow appropriate safety procedures during loading and unloading.

question: If there is a fire on a school bus, the students:
option_a: Must be evacuated.
option_b: Should stay on the bus but be moved to a part of the bus unaffected by the fire.
option_c: Should stay in their seats.
explanation: If a school bus is on fire, or if there is a threat of fire, it is mandatory for a bus driver to evacuate the students from the bus.

question: If a bus must be evacuated, it is safest for students to:
option_a: Stand no more than 50 feet away from the bus.
option_b: Stand downwind of the bus in the event of a fire.
option_c: Be led far away from any railroad tracks.
explanation: After evacuating a school bus, students should be led to a safe place at least 100 feet away from the road in the direction of oncoming traffic. This will keep them safe from flying debris if another vehicle hits the bus. Students should be upwind of any fires and as far away from railroad tracks as possible.

question: After students unload at the school, a driver should:
option_a: Not be concerned with the students' whereabouts.
option_b: Leave after the students have entered the school building.
option_c: Walk through the bus to check for any sleeping students.
explanation: After students unload at school, a school bus driver should walk through the bus to check for sleeping students, hiding students, and items that students may have left behind. Students should exit the bus in an orderly fashion with the driver supervising.

question: If exiting a bus, a driver must:
option_a: Never make contact with the handrail.
option_b: Maintain contact with the handrail.
option_c: Move quickly.
explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

question: When students board a bus, they should:
option_a: Sit in the back row first.
option_b: Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
option_c: Be seated as far from the driver as possible.
explanation: Students should not occupy the back row of a school bus unless the bus is full. The closer to the front of a bus that students are seated, the safer they will be in the event of a rear-end collision. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

question: When taking the basic vehicle control skills test, failing to exit your vehicle properly during any exercise will result in:
option_a: Failure of only that exercise.
option_b: An extra point against your final score.
option_c: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

question: At a passive railroad crossing, the decision to proceed:
option_a: Rests with the driver.
option_b: Is indicated by a control device.
option_c: Is decided by the vehicle in front of you.
explanation: Railroad crossings that do not have any kind of traffic control device are known as passive crossings. The decision to proceed across tracks at a passive crossing is entirely up to the driver.

question: If a student drops an item while approaching a school bus, the student should:
option_a: Stop and pick up the object.
option_b: Have another student pick up the object.
option_c: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
explanation: If a student tries to retrieve a dropped object, they may disappear from the driver's line of sight. This is potentially very dangerous. Rather than retrieve dropped items themselves, students should move to a point of safety outside of the bus's danger zones, get the driver's attention, and wait for the driver to retrieve what has been dropped.

question: As a general rule, student safety is best maintained by:
option_a: Keeping students on the bus.
option_b: Letting some students evacuate the bus.
option_c: Letting students evacuate the bus and scatter.
explanation: In most emergency or crisis situations, students will be safest and easiest to keep under control if they remain on the school bus. Generally, students should be kept on the bus as long as it does not expose them to unnecessary risks or injury.

question: When dropping off students at a school, a driver should:
option_a: Secure the bus by turning off the engine.
option_b: Leave the key in the ignition, if leaving the driver’s compartment.
option_c: Read a book while students unload.
explanation: When unloading students at a school, a bus driver must secure the bus by turning off the engine. If they must leave the driver's compartment, they should remove the key from the ignition. The driver must supervise the unloading process.

question: When performing a pre-trip inspection and looking into the fifth wheel gap, you should:
option_a: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
option_b: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
option_c: Make sure the locking jaws are loose.
explanation: When inspecting a tractor/trailer coupling, look into the fifth wheel gap and make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

question: If taking the driving test and the route does not include a railroad crossing, you:
option_a: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
option_b: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
option_c: Will have to take the test again on a route that does include a railroad crossing.
explanation: If your on-road driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you may be asked to explain and demonstrate the proper railroad crossing procedures to the examiner at a simulated location.

question: When approaching a school bus stop, the bus driver should:
option_a: Not use their mirrors.
option_b: Approach the stop with caution.
option_c: Stop on the sidewalk.
explanation: A school bus driver should always approach bus stops slowly and cautiously.

question: Active railroad crossings:
option_a: Have traffic control devices installed.
option_b: Do not have any traffic control devices installed.
option_c: Are crossed by at least 10 vehicles every hour.
explanation: Railroad crossings with control devices to regulate traffic are known as active crossings. Control devices may include regulators such as flashing red lights, warning bells, and gates. Drivers are required by law to follow instructions given by control devices.

question: When alley docking, you should first:
option_a: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
option_b: Back up directly in front of the alley.
option_c: Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.
explanation: If you are asked to alley dock, you should first pull past the alley and stop your vehicle in a position that is parallel to the outer boundary. From there, you should back your vehicle entirely into the alley parking area. Your vehicle should be parked in a straight position within the boundaries of the parking space.

question: ABS allows you to:
option_a: Drive faster.
option_b: Drive less carefully.
option_c: Maintain control under slippery conditions.
explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) help prevent brake lockup when driving on slippery surfaces. If a driver brakes too hard on a slippery surface, ABS makes it easier for the driver to maintain control of their vehicle. A vehicle equipped with ABS should be driven and braked in the same way as a vehicle without ABS.

question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:
option_a: Swerve to avoid a hazard.
option_b: Parallel park.
option_c: Drive straight into a parking space.
explanation: Maneuvers that may be included in the basic vehicle control skills test include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

question: During the driving test, the examiner will be scoring you on:
option_a: Attitude.
option_b: How quickly you arrive to your destination.
option_c: Your general driving behavior.
explanation: During the on-road driving test, the examiner will be scoring you on specific driving maneuvers, as well as your general driving behavior.

question: If you are stopped at a railroad crossing while operating a school bus, you should:
option_a: Prepare to proceed as soon as a train passes.
option_b: Ignore signs and signals.
option_c: Open the door to listen for approaching trains.
explanation: When stopped at a railroad crossing while operating a school bus, do not rely only on signals to tell you if a train is approaching. You should silence all passengers, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. After a train has passed, you should check for another train approaching from either direction before you proceed across the tracks.

question: As a general rule, where should students be kept during an emergency?
option_a: On the bus
option_b: On the side of the road near the bus
option_c: In a field away from the bus
explanation: In most emergency or crisis situations, students on a school bus will be safer and more easily controlled if they are kept on the bus than if they are evacuated. However, if staying on a bus will expose the students to risk or injury, the bus driver should escort them to a safe location.

question: If a student drops an item near a stopped bus, they should:
option_a: Hurry and pick up the item.
option_b: Leave the item behind.
option_c: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
option_d: Have another student pick it up.
explanation: It is dangerous for students to retrieve dropped items because doing so could cause them to disappear from the driver's view at a crucial moment. If an item is dropped, the student should get out of the bus's danger zones, get the attention of the driver, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is considered an encroachment?
option_a: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
option_b: A driver executing a single pull-up.
option_c: A driver placing the vehicle in neutral and applying the parking brake.
option_d: The vehicle stalling while the driver shifts gears.
explanation: An encroachment during the basic vehicle control skills test is when an exercise boundary line is touched or crossed by any portion of the applicant's vehicle. Every encroachment will be counted as an error.

question: Before operating a school bus, ____ should be checked.
option_a: The left mirror
option_b: The right mirror
option_c: All mirrors
option_d: The inside mirror
explanation: It is essential that school bus drivers check all of the bus's mirrors before operating the vehicle. You should always have a maximum viewing area that is consistent with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. If necessary, have the positioning of the mirrors adjusted.

question: While students load and unload a bus, the driver should:
option_a: Read a book.
option_b: Watch the process and keep an eye on the students.
option_c: Talk to other bus drivers.
option_d: Listen to the radio.
explanation: The driver of a school bus should observe students as they enter or exit the bus to ensure that they are not caught in the door or handrails. It is also important to make sure the students have moved a safe distance away from the unloading area after they have exited the bus.

question: When conducting a vehicle inspection, you must show each of the following, except:
option_a: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
option_b: That the oil pressure warning light turns off, or that the gauge shows increasing or normal oil pressure.
option_c: That the oil temperature gauge, if equipped, rises to the normal operating range.
option_d: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge as part of a vehicle inspection test, you must ensure that it is working. The gauge should show increasing or normal oil pressure, or the oil pressure warning light should turn off. If equipped with one, the oil temperature gauge should begin a gradual rise to the normal operating range.

question: When asked to make a lane change during the skills test, you should:
option_a: Make the necessary traffic checks first.
option_b: Not use your mirrors.
option_c: Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow the instructions.
option_d: Not make the lane change if you don’t want to.
explanation: You will be asked to make multiple lane changes during the driving skills test. Before changing lanes, you should make the necessary traffic checks and use proper signals. Change lanes smoothly when you can do so safely.

question: During the skills test, if making a turn that requires a stop, you should:
option_a: Skid to a stop.
option_b: Stop after the stop line to get a better view.
option_c: Allow your vehicle to roll.
option_d: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
explanation: If you must come to a stop before making a turn during the driving skills test, you should come to a smooth stop behind any stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels aimed straight ahead and do not let your vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you are still able to see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:
option_a: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
option_b: A pull-up should be completed at least once.
option_c: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
option_d: Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.
explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, a pull-up will be scored any time an applicant stops and pulls forward to gain a better position. Stopping without changing direction will not. An excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.

question: When checking tire condition during the vehicle inspection, you should:
option_a: Ensure that the insides of the tires are more worn than the outsides of the tires.
option_b: Ensure that the outsides of the tires are more worn than the insides of the tires.
option_c: Ensure that the middles of the tires are more worn than the outsides of the tires.
option_d: Ensure that the tires have even wear.
explanation: When examining your tires during the vehicle inspection test, you should ensure that treads are evenly worn.

question: Drivers should try to stop ____ away from students at a bus stop.
option_a: About 100 feet
option_b: At least 50 feet
option_c: At least 10 feet
option_d: Less than 10 feet
explanation: A school bus should stop at least 10 feet away from students who are being picked up at a bus stop. This forces the students to walk toward the bus, allowing the driver to observe their movements and better monitor their locations.

question: When should a bus start moving after students have boarded?
option_a: As soon as the students are through the door
option_b: When the students are near their seats but are still standing
option_c: When the students are seated and looking forward
option_d: As soon as the students cross the standee line
explanation: Once students have boarded a school bus, the driver should wait to move the bus until all of the passengers are seated and looking forward.

question: When asked to complete a driver's side parallel parking maneuver, you should:
option_a: Pass the parking space while backing, then pull forward into it.
option_b: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
option_c: Pull forward into the parking space without passing it first.
option_d: Back into the parking space without passing it first.
explanation: You may be asked to complete a parallel parking maneuver into a parking space that is to the left of your vehicle. You should drive past the parking space before backing into it while bringing the rear of your vehicle as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle should be completely within the boundaries of the space.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing while operating a school bus, you should generally:
option_a: Stop between 15 and 50 feet before the nearest rail.
option_b: Stop 100 feet before the nearest rail.
option_c: Stop 10 feet before the nearest rail.
option_d: Continue across the tracks without stopping.
explanation: In general, school bus drivers should stop before any railroad crossings to check the tracks for approaching trains. Drivers should stop no closer than 15 feet, and no farther than 50 feet, from the nearest rail in order to have the best view of the tracks. They should look and listen for approaching trains before proceeding through the crossing.

question: Properly adjusted outside convex mirrors should allow the driver to see:
option_a: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
option_b: Where the front of each front tire touches the ground.
option_c: The top of the bus.
option_d: The muffler.
explanation: On a school bus, outside convex mirrors should be adjusted to allow the driver to see at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus; the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts; and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

question: Outside flat mirrors should be adjusted to see ____ behind the bus.
option_a: One bus length
option_b: 50 feet
option_c: Four bus lengths
option_d: 1,000 feet
explanation: On a school bus, the outside right and left side mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet (or four bus lengths) behind the bus.

question: If your bus's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working:
option_a: You will not have any working brakes.
option_b: The brakes will react more slowly than usual.
option_c: You will still have normal braking power.
option_d: You should not brake.
explanation: If its Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working, a vehicle will still retain its normal braking power. The driver should continue to drive and brake in a normal fashion.

question: When approaching students at a bus stop, you should stop:
option_a: As close as possible to the students.
option_b: Within an arm’s reach of the students.
option_c: At least 10 feet away from the students.
option_d: About 80 feet away from the students.
explanation: When approaching a bus stop, a school bus driver should come to a full stop at least 10 feet away from the waiting students. By forcing the students to walk to the bus, the driver is better able to keep an eye on their movements and location.

question: A school bus stop:
option_a: Can be added by the driver if there is a need.
option_b: Should be voted on by the students.
option_c: May change, depending on weather conditions.
option_d: Should be established by the proper school district authorities.
explanation: A school bus driver should not alter the location of a bus stop without written authorization of the appropriate school district officials.

question: Outside mirrors on a school bus should be adjusted:
option_a: Before a trip begins.
option_b: During a trip.
option_c: After students board the bus.
option_d: After a trip ends.
explanation: All mirrors on a school bus should be checked and adjusted before beginning a trip. Proper mirror adjustment is vital to the safety of all students and surrounding vehicles.

question: A properly adjusted flat mirror should allow the driver to see:
option_a: The rear tires touching the ground.
option_b: The front tires touching the ground.
option_c: Only the roadway and no parts of the bus.
option_d: The front bumper.
explanation: Properly adjusted flat mirrors on a school bus should allow the driver to see 200 feet behind the bus, the base of each rear wheel, and the sides of the bus.

question: Your vehicle's final position should be:
option_a: Exactly where the examiner has instructed it to be.
option_b: Within five feet of the final position described by the examiner.
option_c: Wherever you can safely park.
option_d: Within two feet of the final position described by the examiner.
explanation: You should finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position described by the examiner. You can be penalized for failing to complete an exercise exactly in the manner described by the examiner, potentially resulting in failure of the basic control skills test.

question: The area to the left of a school bus is considered especially dangerous to students because:
option_a: The sun’s reflection obscures the left side of the bus.
option_b: Passing vehicles are located to the left of the bus.
option_c: It is difficult to see the left side of any bus.
option_d: There is no door on the left side of the bus.
explanation: While all sides of a school bus have danger zones, the left side is particularly hazardous to students due to the presence of passing vehicles.

question: If asked to sight-side back your vehicle into an alley, you should first:
option_a: Pull directly into the alley parking space.
option_b: Turn your vehicle to the right to position yourself directly in front of the alley.
option_c: Pull past the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer boundary.
option_d: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
explanation: If you are asked to alley dock, you should first pull past the alley and stop your vehicle in a position that is parallel to the outer boundary. From there, you should back your vehicle entirely into the alley parking area. Your vehicle should be parked in a straight position within the boundaries of the parking space.

question: In the event of a bus evacuation, students should be led at least ____ away from the road.
option_a: 10 feet
option_b: 20 feet
option_c: 50 feet
option_d: 100 feet
explanation: If it is necessary to evacuate a school bus, students should be led by the driver in the direction of oncoming traffic to a safe location that is at least 100 feet off the road. This will help to ensure that they are not hit by flying debris if another vehicle hits the bus.

question: After students unload at a school, the driver:
option_a: May assume students have taken all of their belongings with them.
option_b: Should assume the students have immediately cleared the doorway.
option_c: Should walk through the bus and check for any sleeping or hiding students.
option_d: May turn off the dispatch radio.
explanation: After students have exited a bus at a school, the driver should walk through the bus to check for any remaining students who are hiding or sleeping. Drivers should also look out for items that students may have left behind.

question: A school bus must be evacuated if:
option_a: The bus has stalled in winter weather conditions.
option_b: The air conditioning system has broken.
option_c: There is any imminent danger of collision.
option_d: Students are getting motion sickness.
explanation: During emergency situations, it is usually safest for students to remain on a school bus. Evacuations are mandatory if the bus has stalled on railroad tracks, if the bus is on fire or there is a threat of fire, or if there is a hazardous materials spill. Students should be evacuated any time there is imminent danger of collision.

question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
option_a: Be swept clean.
option_b: Contain rags.
option_c: Not be used for cargo.
option_d: Be free of cracks.
explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer as a part of the vehicle inspection test, check the front area of the trailer for signs of damage, such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

question: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test:
option_a: Applicants will not have to identify the ABS.
option_b: Windshield wipers are not to be addressed.
option_c: Shock absorbers only need to be checked on one axle.
option_d: The steering box should be checked for leaks.
explanation: During the external inspection portion of the pre-trip vehicle inspection test, you must verify that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking.

question: If a bus is equipped with outside convex mirrors, they will be located:
option_a: Below the outside flat mirrors.
option_b: Above the outside flat mirrors.
option_c: Next to the door.
option_d: On top of the bus.
explanation: Outside convex mirrors on a school bus are located below the outside flat mirrors. They are used to see a wide view of traffic, clearance, and students around the bus.

question: When taking the on-road driving test, you will be evaluated on your lane usage. Which of the following is an example of poor lane usage?
option_a: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
option_b: Stopping behind crosswalks
option_c: Driving in the leftmost lane if more than one driving lane is available
option_d: Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane
explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, make sure you do not put your vehicle over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs. On multiple-lane roads, complete turns in the proper lane. Always move to or remain in the rightmost lane, unless the lane is blocked.

question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:
option_a: Wear your safety belt.
option_b: Obey all traffic laws.
option_c: Complete the test without a moving violation.
option_d: Obey all traffic signs and signals, but only if other traffic is present.
explanation: You must drive in a safe and responsible manner during the on-road driving test. This includes wearing your safety belt; obeying all traffic signs, signals, and laws; and completing the test without an accident or moving violation.

question: If exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:
option_a: Keep both hands on the handrail.
option_b: Not touch the handrail.
option_c: Maintain a firm grasp on the handrail.
option_d: Rush down the stairs.
explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

question: When stopped at a railroad crossing while operating a school bus, you should:
option_a: Assume you'll hear an approaching train.
option_b: Rely solely on signals to tell you if a train is approaching.
option_c: Open the door and listen for a train.
option_d: Immediately proceed after a train has passed.
explanation: When stopped at a railroad crossing while operating a school bus, do not rely only on signals to tell you if a train is approaching. You should silence all passengers, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. After a train has passed, you should check for another train approaching from either direction before you proceed across the tracks.

question: If your vehicle is equipped with a cargo lift, you should ensure that:
option_a: The lift is loosely attached.
option_b: The lift is not leaking.
option_c: The lift is fully extended.
option_d: The lift is the proper color.
explanation: When checking a cargo lift as part of your vehicle inspection test, you should check for leaking, damaged, or missing parts. The lift must be fully retracted and latched securely.

question: When taking the on-road test, you will be evaluated on regular traffic checks. You should not:
option_a: Scan the road for pedestrians.
option_b: Check traffic regularly.
option_c: Avoid checking your mirrors near intersections.
option_d: Check your mirrors regularly.
explanation: While taking the on-road driving skills test, check for traffic and use your mirrors regularly, especially when encountering intersections. Scan and check for pedestrians in areas where they may be present.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
option_a: Not stop.
option_b: Try to pass slower vehicles.
option_c: Change lanes.
option_d: Put the vehicle in neutral.
explanation: When crossing railroad tracks during the on-road driving skills test, you must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the railroad crossing.

question: Students should board a school bus:
option_a: In a single-file line.
option_b: Two at a time.
option_c: In as large a group as possible.
option_d: However they want to. It makes no difference.
explanation: Students should board a school bus slowly while in a single-file line and holding the handrails.

question: When you are approaching a bus stop, the students on your bus should:
option_a: Remain seated.
option_b: Stand up and collect their belongings.
option_c: Walk to the front of the bus and prepare to exit.
option_d: Ask the driver questions.
explanation: Students on a school bus should remain seated until they are told otherwise. It is unsafe for students to walk around the bus while it is moving.

question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:
option_a: Switch lanes frequently.
option_b: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
option_c: Drive on the left side of the lane.
option_d: Drive above the posted speed limit.
explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, you may be asked to drive on an expressway. Make sure you maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed. Continue to thoroughly check traffic in all directions while on the expressway.

question: During the basic control skills test, you can acquire points by:
option_a: Crossing over an exercise boundary.
option_b: Pulling up one time.
option_c: Exiting the vehicle one time to check your positioning.
option_d: Setting the parking brake.
explanation: The examiner will score the number of times your vehicle touches or crosses an exercise boundary line. Each encroachment will count as an error, resulting in points against your skills test score.

question: When checking the power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, you will need to do each of the following, except:
option_a: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
option_b: Check for adequate power steering fluid.
option_c: Ensure that the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
option_d: Ensure that the power steering level is above the refill mark.
explanation: When checking the power steering fluid during the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to indicate where the power steering fluid dipstick is located and show that there is an adequate amount of power steering fluid in the engine compartment. The fluid level must be above the refill mark.

question: When asked to complete an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:
option_a: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
option_b: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
option_c: Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
option_d: Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.
explanation: If you are asked to complete an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should first pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the boundaries of the parking space.

question: When taking the basic control skills test, drivers are:
option_a: Not permitted to stop and exit the vehicle to look at the vehicle’s position.
option_b: Encouraged not to exit the vehicle to look at the vehicle’s position.
option_c: Allowed to leave the vehicle, but only if the vehicle is placed in reverse.
option_d: Allowed to leave the vehicle, but only if the vehicle is placed in neutral and the parking brake is set.
explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you must place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before exiting the vehicle to check its position. You may check the position of the vehicle no more than twice, except during the straight line backing exercise, where you may look no more than once.

question: School buses:
option_a: Are never equipped with ABS.
option_b: Are only equipped with ABS if located in cold climates.
option_c: May be equipped with ABS.
explanation: Most commercial vehicles manufactured after 1998 or 1999 are required to be equipped with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Many older buses are also equipped with ABS.

question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is considered a look?
option_a: Walking to the back of a vehicle to check its position
option_b: Using side mirrors to check a vehicle's position
option_c: Looking out of the driver's side window to check a vehicle's position
option_d: A driver glancing over their shoulder to check blind spots
explanation: A driver uses a look when they open their door, leave their seated position, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During the straight line backing exercise, a driver may not exceed one look. During any other exercise, a driver may not exceed two looks.

question: When taking the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:
option_a: Wear your safety belt.
option_b: Obey all traffic signs.
option_c: Complete the test without an accident.
option_d: Demonstrate that you can use your cell phone while driving.
explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive in a safe and responsible manner; wear your safety belt; obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws; and complete the test without any accidents or moving violations.

question: When inspecting engine compartment belts during the vehicle inspection test:
option_a: The belts should be checked for snugness, each with up to three inches of play.
option_b: The water pump belt does not need to be identified.
option_c: The air compressor belt should be removed.
option_d: The applicant must identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.
explanation: When checking the engine compartment during the vehicle inspection test, you must check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts. In addition to cracks and frays, you should check the belts for snugness, allowing up to three-quarters of an inch of play at the center of each belt. If any of these items are not belt-driven, you must identify them and ensure that their components are operating properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

question: When exiting your vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.
option_a: One point of contact
option_b: Four points of contact
option_c: Three points of contact
option_d: Two points of contact
explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

question: When students are being picked up by a school bus:
option_a: The students should wait at a designated bus stop.
option_b: The driver should pick up students whether or not they are at the designated bus stop.
option_c: The parents should choose where the bus stop will be located.
explanation: A school bus driver should load and unload students only at designated stops that have been approved by appropriate school district officials.

question: When asked to complete an offset back/left parking maneuver, you should:
option_a: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
option_b: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
option_c: Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
option_d: Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.
explanation: If you are asked to complete an offset back/left parking maneuver, you should first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the boundaries of the parking space.

question: When alley docking, your vehicle should be parked:
option_a: With the front bumper on top of the front boundary line.
option_b: With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
option_c: Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
option_d: At an angle within the boundaries of the parking space.
explanation: If you are asked to alley dock, you should first pull past the alley and stop your vehicle in a position that is parallel to the outer boundary. From there, you should back your vehicle entirely into the alley parking area. Your vehicle should be parked in a straight position within the boundaries of the parking space.

question: During the on-road driving test, you should:
option_a: Develop your own route to show off your driving skills.
option_b: Listen to directions from the examiner.
option_c: Bring a passenger to ride with you.
option_d: Drive in an unsafe manner.
explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must listen to and follow the directions given by the examiner. They will never ask you to drive in an unsafe manner.

question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be required to do all of the following, except:
option_a: Walk around the vehicle.
option_b: Point to or touch each item.
option_c: Explain what you are checking and why.
option_d: Crawl under the vehicle.
explanation: As a part of earning your CDL, you will have to pass an inspection test and demonstrate that your vehicle is safe for operation. During the vehicle inspection test, you will have to walk around the vehicle and point to or touch each item and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why. You will not have to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

question: Once stopped as a part of the stop/start maneuver, you should:
option_a: Use the four-way flashers.
option_b: Not use the four-way flashers because it is just a test, not an emergency.
option_c: Leave the vehicle in first gear.
option_d: Park in front of a fire hydrant.
explanation: Once you have stopped as a part of the stop/start maneuver during the on-road driving skills test, you must activate your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. You must not block any driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

question: When checking the springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following, except:
option_a: Look for missing leaf springs.
option_b: Look for broken coil springs.
option_c: Ensure torsion springs are not damaged.
option_d: Glue cracked leaf springs.
explanation: When checking the springs as part of the vehicle inspection test, you should look for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs, as well as broken or distorted coil springs. If the vehicle is equipped with torsion bars, torque arms, or other types of suspension components, ensure that they are not damaged and are mounted securely.

question: Why should a school bus stop a short distance from students who are waiting to board?
option_a: The students will have to walk to the bus, making it easier for the driver to watch their movements.
option_b: The students will usually be waiting on a sidewalk.
option_c: The students may get scared of a school bus coming toward them.
option_d: Buses are difficult to drive.
explanation: When being stopped to load students, a school bus should stop at least 10 feet away from the waiting students. This forces the students to walk toward the bus, making it easier for the driver to keep track of their movements.

question: Before leaving a bus stop, a driver should:
option_a: Make sure no students are running to catch the bus.
option_b: Make sure students have placed their backpacks in the aisle.
option_c: Make sure students have opened the emergency vent.
option_d: Make sure students are facing the rear of the bus.
explanation: Before pulling away from a bus stop, a driver should make sure that there are no students running to catch the bus.

question: When performing a pre-trip inspection, you should make sure that:
option_a: The pedal surface has been smoothed out.
option_b: The gas pedal sticks.
option_c: Nothing is obstrucing the pedals.
option_d: There is something underneath the brake pedal.
explanation: When checking your vehicle's pedals during a pre-trip inspection, you should ensure that there is nothing under or around the pedals that will obstruct their use. Make sure the pedals are in proper working condition and that the surfaces of the pedals are grooved, if applicable.

question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:
option_a: On the outside left of the bus.
option_b: On the outside right of the bus.
option_c: Above the windshield inside the bus.
explanation: In a school bus, the overhead rearview mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver’s side.

question: If a bus has a restroom, the restroom must include:
option_a: An emergency buzzer.
option_b: A window.
option_c: Two exits.
option_d: Paper towels.
explanation: The restroom on a bus must be equipped with an emergency buzzer.

question: The overhead inside rearview mirror:
option_a: Allows the driver to see what is happening inside of the bus.
option_b: Allows the driver to see what is happening outside of the bus.
option_c: Monitors traffic.
option_d: Opens and closes the door.
explanation: In a school bus, the overhead inside rearview mirror is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.

question: At railroad crossings, bus drivers:
option_a: Do not need to stop.
option_b: Do not need to stop, but must reduce their speed to 25 mph below the posted speed limit.
option_c: Do not need to stop, but must open the door to listen for trains.
option_d: Must stop and check for any approaching trains.
explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing while driving a bus, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest track to look and listen for any approaching trains. Only proceed once you are certain that there are no approaching trains. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings; if a police officer or flagger is directing traffic; if there is a green traffic signal at the crossing; or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

question: Buses must never carry ____ in the space occupied by passengers.
option_a: Small arms ammunition
option_b: An oxygen tank
option_c: Radioactive materials
option_d: Passengers who are drunk
explanation: Buses must never carry labeled radioactive materials in the area occupied by passengers.

question: Which of the following is likely to result in the most student deaths per year?
option_a: Students loading and unloading a school bus
option_b: Accidents involving drunk drivers
option_c: Accidents involving negligence
option_d: Accidents in which drivers ignore traffic signals or signs
explanation: More students are killed each year while getting on or off school buses than while riding as passengers on board school buses.

question: When passengers ride a bus:
option_a: Leaving items in the aisle is acceptable.
option_b: Leaving items in the aisle is acceptable while everyone is seated.
option_c: There should be no obstacles in the aisle.
option_d: An item may be left in the aisle if there is an orange cone beside it.
explanation: Do not allow passengers to leave any items in an aisle while the bus is moving. Aisles and stairwells should always be free of obstructions.

question: Before driving a bus that has been left unattended:
option_a: The vehicle should be thoroughly washed.
option_b: Air should be removed from tires.
option_c: The interior should be checked for damage.
option_d: The driver should look for any animals that may have gotten onboard.
explanation: People sometimes damage unattended buses. When inspecting a bus that has been left unattended, you should do a walkthrough to check the interior for damage.

question: Before driving a bus, you must:
option_a: Review its most recent inspection report.
option_b: Wash the outside.
option_c: Clean the interior.
option_d: Count the seats.
explanation: A bus must always be inspected before it is driven. The inspection process must include a review of the inspection report made by the previous driver. You should operate the vehicle only if defects listed on the inspection report have been certified as repaired or as not needing to be repaired.

question: Before operating a bus, you should ensure that it is safe by:
option_a: Reviewing the inspection report left by the previous driver.
option_b: Kicking the tires.
option_c: Asking your supervisor if the bus seems safe.
option_d: Asking passengers if they are comfortable.
explanation: A bus must always be inspected before it is driven. The inspection process must include a review of the inspection report made by the previous driver. You should operate the vehicle only if defects listed on the inspection report have been certified as repaired or as not needing to be repaired.

question: Buses must never carry:
option_a: Small arms ammunition.
option_b: Soft drinks.
option_c: Medical supplies.
option_d: Tear gas.
explanation: While some kinds of hazardous materials may be carried on a bus under certain conditions, tear gas and irritating materials must never be carried. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D and emergency medical supplies are permitted.

question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?
option_a: One
option_b: Three
option_c: Six
option_d: Nine
explanation: A hazardous material will be placed into one of nine classes to explain the type of risks associated with the material.

question: If a bus has a brake and accelerator interlock system, the system should:
option_a: Be turned off in most situations.
option_b: Only be used in inclement weather.
option_c: Never be used in place of the parking brake.
option_d: Operate the rear door.
explanation: Urban transit buses may have a brake and accelerator interlock system, which applies the brakes and holds the throttle in an idle position while the rear door is open. This system should not be used as a substitute for the parking brake.

question: If driving a charter bus, a driver should:
option_a: Tell passengers how to operate the TVs, if equipped.
option_b: Not allow passengers to board until the scheduled departure time.
option_c: Allow passengers to board early to get ahead of schedule.
option_d: Tell passengers to fill the back of the bus first.
explanation: To help prevent theft or vandalism, charter bus drivers should not allow passengers to board the vehicle until the scheduled departure time.

question: The loading of a school bus:
option_a: Is not a dangerous process.
option_b: Does not need to be supervised.
option_c: Should be done quickly.
option_d: Can be dangerous.
explanation: More students are killed each year during loading or unloading of school buses than while riding on school buses. Therefore, it is critical that school bus drivers follow appropriate safety procedures during loading and unloading.

question: If you miss a student’s stop while bringing students home after school, you should:
option_a: Back up to the stop.
option_b: Follow locally established procedures.
option_c: Not worry about the student.
option_d: Stop quickly and let them exit.
explanation: If a school bus driver forgets to stop where a student is meant to unload, the driver should not back up to the stop. Instead, they should follow established local procedures.

question: Rules regarding passenger comfort, such as smoking guidelines, should:
option_a: Not be mentioned unless there is a rule violation.
option_b: Only be mentioned if a passenger specifically asks about something.
option_c: Be announced at the start of the trip.
option_d: Be discussed individually with each passenger.
explanation: Many charter and intercity carriers have rules about passengers smoking, drinking, and using music players while on the bus. Explaining passenger rules at the start of a trip is often an effective way to avoid trouble later on.

question: The stairwell of a bus:
option_a: Can be used to store items, if needed.
option_b: Can be used as a seat, if needed.
option_c: Should be used to store small items.
option_d: Must remain clear at all times.
explanation: The aisles and stairwell of a bus must be kept clear at all times. Do not let passengers use these areas to store additional baggage.

question: In general, a disabled bus with passengers still on board:
option_a: Should be pushed by another bus.
option_b: Should not be pushed by another bus.
option_c: Should be towed.
option_d: Should be abandoned.
explanation: A disabled bus with riders on board should not be towed or pushed by another vehicle, unless it would be unsafe for the passengers to exit the bus in the location where it is stranded. If that is the case, the bus may be towed or pushed to a safe location for passengers to exit the bus.

question: If a school bus needs to be evacuated, passengers should:
option_a: Always use the rear door.
option_b: Always use the windows.
option_c: Always use the front door.
option_d: Use the exit deemed safest.
explanation: If a school bus needs to be evacuated in the event of an emergency, the driver must quickly determine which exit or exits will be safest for students to use and direct the students to that exit.

question: An outside convex mirror is properly adjusted if:
option_a: The driver can see at least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
option_b: The driver can see the front bumper.
option_c: The driver can see the top of the bus.
option_d: The driver can see the front windshield.
explanation: The outside right and left side convex mirrors on a school bus should be positioned so that the driver can see the fronts of the rear tires touching the ground; each side of the bus up to the mirror mounts; and at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus.

question: When arriving at a destination, a bus driver should:
option_a: Not communicate with passengers.
option_b: Be quiet.
option_c: Wait to make announcements until the bus has stopped and passengers are exiting.
option_d: Remind exiting passengers to take their belongings.
explanation: When arriving at a final destination or intermediate stop, a bus driver should remind passengers to take their belongings with them when exiting the bus. It is best for the driver to make this announcement before the bus comes to a complete stop.

question: What do outside crossover mirrors allow a driver to see?
option_a: The front bumper
option_b: The rear bumper
option_c: The right side of the bus
option_d: The left side of the bus
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to help a school bus driver see the danger zone area directly in front of the bus, as well as the danger zone areas to the left and right sides of the bus, including the area from the front of the bus to the service door.

question: Buses should never transport:
option_a: Medical drugs.
option_b: Small arms ammunition.
option_c: Emergency hospital supplies.
option_d: Radioactive materials.
explanation: Buses must never transport labeled radioactive materials in the space occupied by people. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and medications are allowed.

question: The driver’s seat of a bus should include:
option_a: A pocket for storage on its left side.
option_b: A pocket for storage on its right side.
option_c: A seat belt.
option_d: A cup holder.
explanation: The driver's seat on a bus must be equipped with a seat belt, which the driver should always use.

question: When planning to drive a bus that has been parked for a few days:
option_a: The driver should assume the interior is in good working order.
option_b: The driver should call the local police department.
option_c: The driver should do a walkthrough inspection to ensure no damage has occurred since the last trip.
option_d: The driver should ask the passengers to check the interior of the bus.
explanation: People sometimes damage unattended buses. Before driving a bus that has been unattended, you should check the interior to confirm that everything is in proper condition.

question: Carry-on luggage should be:
option_a: Stored in the aisle.
option_b: Kept on the laps of the passengers.
option_c: Kept near the doorway.
option_d: Secured in a way that allows the driver to move freely and easily.
explanation: On a bus, all baggage and freight must be stored in a manner that allows the driver to move freely and easily; allows riders to exit by any window or door in the event of an emergency; and protects riders from injury if the items fall or shift.

question: Many carriers have passenger and safety rules. To avoid issues with passengers reacting to these rules, you should:
option_a: Not transport any passengers.
option_b: Not have passengers sit next to each other.
option_c: Have passengers who may want to smoke sit next to each other.
option_d: Explain the rules at the start of the trip.
explanation: Many charter and intercity carriers have rules about passengers smoking, drinking, and using music players while on the bus. Explaining passenger rules at the start of a trip is often an effective way to avoid trouble later on.

question: An emergency roof hatch:
option_a: Must always be locked down before traveling.
option_b: May be left partially open while traveling to allow for the movement of fresh air.
option_c: Should never be opened, except in an emergency.
option_d: Should always be open while traveling.
explanation: While emergency roof hatches on buses may be locked in partially-open positions to allow for the movement of fresh air, do not leave them open as a regular practice. It is important to remember that having a hatch open gives the bus a slightly higher clearance.

question: One reason for you to sign a previous driver’s vehicle inspection report is if:
option_a: The previous driver dated their entry.
option_b: Reported defects are certified to have been repaired.
option_c: You plan to drive for longer than one hour or travel farther than 50 miles.
option_d: The report is left on the dashboard.
explanation: You should only sign a previous inspection report if defects were either noted and certified to have been repaired or if repairs were not needed.

question: The emergency exit door:
option_a: Can be opened if the bus becomes too hot while being driven.
option_b: Can be opened while the bus is being driven if the bus is carrying cargo.
option_c: Can be opened to provide a better view while the bus is being backed.
option_d: Should never be open while the bus is being driven.
explanation: Check all emergency exits before operating a bus. Never drive a bus with an open emergency exit door or window.

question: When should you inspect the mirrors on a bus?
option_a: Before operating the bus
option_b: While operating the bus
option_c: After operating the bus
option_d: Is not necessary to inspect the mirrors.
explanation: The mirrors of a bus should always be inspected before a trip. Adjust them as necessary before beginning to drive.

question: When completing a conventional parallel parking maneuver, you should:
option_a: Back up past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
option_b: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
option_c: Pull forward directly into the parking space.
explanation: You may be asked to complete a conventional parallel parking maneuver into a parking space that is to the right of your vehicle. You should drive past the parking space before backing into it while bringing the rear of your vehicle as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle should be completely within the boundaries of the space.

question: If students on the bus cause a disturbance while other students are unloading, what should you do?
option_a: Immediately walk to the back of the bus and take care of the disturbance while students unload.
option_b: Wait until the students are done unloading and then take care of the disturbance.
option_c: Have a student who is closer to the disturbance handle the situation while you supervise unloading.
explanation: The process of loading or unloading students from a school bus requires a driver's full concentration. If there is a behavioral issue on the bus, wait until the exiting students are safely off the bus and out of the way before you address the problem on the bus.

question: Adjust a bus's mirrors:
option_a: Before operating the bus.
option_b: While operating the bus.
option_c: At the first stoplight after starting your shift.
explanation: The adjustment of mirrors should be checked prior to the start of any trip.

question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:
option_a: Differently each time in order to place emphasis on different items.
option_b: The same way each time to prevent you from forgetting anything.
option_c: Once in a while.
explanation: A pre-trip inspection should be completed in the same way before every drive. Consistency will help you learn all of the proper steps and decrease the likelihood that you will forget to check something.

question: Students loading and unloading a bus:
option_a: Is simple and does not need to be supervised.
option_b: Can be dangerous and should be supervised.
option_c: May be done without the bus driver present.
explanation: More students are killed each year during loading or unloading of school buses than while riding on school buses. Therefore, it is critical that school bus drivers follow appropriate safety procedures during loading and unloading. This process should never take place without being properly supervised.

question: If your vehicle's ABS is malfunctioning:
option_a: You will not have any working brakes.
option_b: You will still have brakes.
option_c: You should only use the parking brake.
explanation: Anti-lock brakes are meant to keep a vehicle's wheels from locking up during hard applications. If your vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) malfunctions, its standard braking functions should still be in place. You should continue to drive and brake in a normal manner.

question: When stopping to pick up students, be sure to park at least 10 feet away from the students because:
option_a: You will have a good view of their movements.
option_b: It will be difficult to get any closer to the students.
option_c: Students should walk for exercise.
explanation: When picking up passengers, a school bus driver should park with the vehicle's front bumper at least 10 feet away from the students. This is the safest parking option because it forces the students to walk to the bus, making it possible for the driver to watch their movements.

question: If you come to railroad tracks while driving a school bus, you should generally:
option_a: Check the tracks, but continue driving without stopping.
option_b: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
option_c: Stop 75 feet before the nearest rail.
explanation: In general, school bus drivers should stop before any railroad crossings to check the tracks for approaching trains. Drivers should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail in order to have the best view of the tracks. They should look and listen for approaching trains before proceeding through the crossing.

question: Doors should be closed while a school bus is being driven, except when:
option_a: Crossing railroad tracks.
option_b: Needing to cool off the inside of the vehicle.
option_c: There is no vehicle next to the bus.
explanation: The doors of a school bus must be kept closed any time the bus is moving, except when it is crossing railroad tracks.

question: If you are taking the driving test and the route does not include a railroad crossing, you:
option_a: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
option_b: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
option_c: Will have to take a different route.
explanation: During the on-road driving test, if your route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and demonstrate the necessary procedures at a simulated location.

question: When operating a school bus, mirrors should be adjusted:
option_a: During the drive.
option_b: Before beginning to drive.
option_c: After the drive is completed.
explanation: It is critical to the safe operation of a school bus that mirrors be properly adjusted. Always check each mirror before operating the bus.

question: If a gate controlling a railroad crossing does not go back up after a train passes, you should:
option_a: Drive around the gate.
option_b: Wait for another vehicle to cross the tracks first to see if it is safe.
option_c: Call your dispatcher.
explanation: If you are stopped at a railroad crossing and a gate fails to return to its open position after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not attempt to drive around the lowered gate.

question: When exiting a vehicle, it is important to maintain ____ with your vehicle at all times.
option_a: Three points of contact
option_b: Four points of contact
option_c: Two points of contact
explanation: As you exit your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

question: If you must drive in reverse at a student pick-up point, you should:
option_a: Back up before the students board the bus.
option_b: Back up after the students board the bus.
option_c: Back up while students direct you.
explanation: Backing in a school bus is strongly discouraged and should be done only if there is no other safe way to move the vehicle. If you must drive in reverse at a student pick-up point, you should wait until all students have first loaded the bus.

question: Before evacuating a bus in response to a hazard, a driver should:
option_a: Ask the students if they want to leave.
option_b: Explain the situation to the dispatcher.
option_c: Take their time deciding if an evacuation is necessary.
explanation: If time permits, before deciding to evacuate a school bus, the driver should contact their dispatcher to explain the situation. The decision to evacuate must be a timely one.

question: When students board a school bus, the driver should:
option_a: Read a book.
option_b: Check all mirrors.
option_c: Only look at the students.
explanation: While students are boarding a school bus, the driver should supervise the loading while watching all mirrors for any students running to catch the bus.

question: When boarding a school bus, students should:
option_a: Be in a single-file line.
option_b: Be in pairs.
option_c: Not use the handrail.
explanation: Students should board a school bus slowly and in a single-file line. For safety, boarding students should use the handrail.

question: A passive railroad crossing:
option_a: Has a control device.
option_b: Does not have any control devices.
option_c: Should be avoided.
explanation: Railroad crossings that do not display any traffic control devices are known as passive crossings. The decision to proceed across tracks at a passive crossing is entirely up to the driver.

question: A post-trip inspection should include all of the following, except:
option_a: Looking for articles left on the bus.
option_b: Checking for sleeping students.
option_c: Opening windows.
explanation: After completing a trip, a school bus driver should do an inspection in which they check for sleeping students; belongings left on the bus; open windows or doors; any mechanical or operational issues with the bus; and damage or vandalism.

question: When asked to make a lane change during the driving test, you should:
option_a: Make the change as soon as the examiner asks, without looking.
option_b: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
option_c: Make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.
explanation: You will be asked to change lanes during the on-road driving test. When the examiner asks you to do this, you should make the necessary traffic checks and use the proper signals before changing lanes.

question: The overhead inside rearview mirror should be positioned to show:
option_a: The rear tires.
option_b: All of the students on the bus.
option_c: The floor of the bus.
explanation: The top portion of the overhead inside rearview mirror should be positioned to display the top of the bus's rear window. This mirror positioning should allow the driver to see all of the students on the bus, including the heads of the students sitting immediately behind the driver.

question: When stopping to pick up students, a bus driver should:
option_a: Place the vehicle in park.
option_b: Place the vehicle in first gear.
option_c: Place the vehicle in reverse.
option_d: Place the vehicle in third gear.
explanation: When stopping to pick up students, a school bus should be put in park. If the transmission does not have a park shift point, the vehicle should instead be placed in neutral.

question: What happens if a driver exceeds the number of permitted looks during any particular exercise?
option_a: They must restart the exercise.
option_b: They will automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.
option_c: They will fail only that particular exercise.
option_d: Three points will be marked against their test score.
explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test exercises, a driver may leave their seated position and check the positioning of their vehicle. Using such a look more than two times during any exercise (except the straight line backing exercise) will result in an automatic failure of the skills test. Using such a look more than once during the straight line backing exercise will result in automatic failure.

question: What should properly adjusted outside side flat mirrors on a school bus allow the driver to see?
option_a: The sides of the school bus
option_b: Under the school bus
option_c: The front tires touching the ground
option_d: Vehicles in front of the bus
explanation: When properly adjusted, the outside side flat mirrors on a school bus should allow the driver to see along the sides of the bus; the rear tires touching the ground; and 200 feet behind the bus.

question: During exercises that are not the straight line backing exercise, you may exit your vehicle to check its position no more than:
option_a: One time.
option_b: Two times.
option_c: Three times.
option_d: Four times.
explanation: A driver is allowed to exit their vehicle to check its position during any basic control skills test exercise. This action is called a "look." During the straight line backing exercise, a driver may not exceed one look. During any other exercise, a driver may not exceed two looks.

question: An active railroad crossing:
option_a: Has a traffic control device installed at the crossing.
option_b: Does not have any traffic control devices installed at the crossing.
option_c: Is characterized by having at least 10 vehicles cross the tracks every hour.
option_d: Should be avoided.
explanation: Active railroad crossings use installed traffic control devices to regulate traffic. These devices can be in the form of flashing red lights, warning bells, and/or gates. The directions of devices controlling railroad crossings must always be followed.

question: Buses may carry:
option_a: Small arms ammunition.
option_b: Corrosive materials.
option_c: Poison gas.
option_d: Explosives other than small arms ammunition.
explanation: Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs are permitted to be transported by bus. Most other kinds of hazardous materials may not be carried on buses.

question: During a vehicle inspection, be sure that:
option_a: The emergency exits are difficult to open.
option_b: The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
option_c: The emergency exits squeak.
option_d: The emergency exits are not accessible from inside the cab.
explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must ensure that any emergency exit warning devices are working. All emergency exits should operate smoothly, be undamaged, and close securely from the inside.

question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times are you permitted to exit the vehicle to check its position?
option_a: One time
option_b: Two times
option_c: Three times
option_d: Four times
explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you are permitted to exit your vehicle to check its position no more than one time.

question: When asked about the vehicle's oil during the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following, except:
option_a: Indicate where the dipstick is located.
option_b: Show that the oil level is within a safe operating range.
option_c: Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
option_d: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to indicate where the oil dipstick is located; show that the oil level is within a safe operating range; and show that the oil level is above the refill mark.

question: If a driver cannot account for a student after the student has exited the bus, the driver should:
option_a: Secure and leave the bus to look for the student.
option_b: Assume the student has safely exited the bus.
option_c: Walk to the back of the bus to see if the student got back on.
option_d: Ask another student if they've seen the student.
explanation: During unloading, if a school bus driver cannot account for a student outside of the bus, they should secure the bus and check for the missing student around and underneath the bus.

question: A posted speed limit that is safe for cars:
option_a: Is usually safe to be driven by buses.
option_b: May be too fast for a bus.
option_c: May be too slow for a bus.
option_d: Should be thought of as the minimum speed limit.
explanation: Posted speed limits on roadways, especially through turns and curves, may be safe for cars but too fast for buses. Drivers of large vehicles should be aware of how fast their vehicle can safely be driven.

question: Before driving a bus that has been parked for a few days:
option_a: The driver should assume the interior is in good working order.
option_b: The driver should call the local police department.
option_c: The driver should complete a walkthrough inspection.
option_d: The driver should ask the passengers to check the interior of the bus.
explanation: People sometimes damage unattended buses, so before driving a bus that has been idle, you should complete a walkthrough of the interior to ensure that it will be safe for riders.

question: When inspecting the interior of a bus, you should:
option_a: Loosen every seat.
option_b: Check every handhold.
option_c: Assume all buzzers work properly.
option_d: Remove the emergency exit handles.
explanation: When inspecting the interior of a bus, you must make sure everything is safe and in proper working condition. Take the time to ensure every handhold and railing is securely in place and safe to use.

question: If equipped with flashing lights, how far in advance of a school bus stop should the bus's lights be activated?
option_a: At least 50 feet
option_b: At least 100 feet
option_c: At least 200 feet
option_d: At least 1,000 feet
explanation: If a school bus is equipped with alternating flashing amber warning lights, they should be activated at least 200 feet before a stop, unless state law requires otherwise.

question: If equipped, a header board should:
option_a: Be damaged.
option_b: Be loose.
option_c: Be strong enough to contain cargo.
option_d: Light up when the engine is started.
explanation: When checking a header board during the vehicle inspection test, you should ensure that it is secure, free of damage, and strong enough to contain cargo.

question: About how many seconds in advance of a bus stop should warning lights be activated?
option_a: One to two seconds
option_b: Two to four seconds
option_c: Five to ten seconds
option_d: 45 seconds
explanation: If a school bus is equipped with alternating amber warning lights, they must be activated at least 200 feet, or about five to ten seconds, before the stop.

question: If a student drops an item while approaching the bus, the student should:
option_a: Stop and pick up the object.
option_b: Have another student pick up the object.
option_c: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
option_d: Just leave the item alone and walk away.
explanation: It is dangerous for students to retrieve dropped items because doing so could cause them to disappear from the driver's view at a crucial moment. If an item is dropped, the student should get out of the bus's danger zones, get the attention of the driver, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

question: The boarding of passengers onto a school bus:
